newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Nelson field to up output next week-operator.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Nelson field to up output next week-operator.

text.p: The North Sea's Nelson field is expected to start raising output to about 140,000 barrels per day this coming weekend following repairs to a gas compressor, an official at operator Enterprise Oil said on Tuesday.

The official said the repaired compressor would probably be restarted on Friday, and production would rise over the following few days to around 140,000 barrels per day from current output of about 53,000 bpd.
The official declined to say when full capacity might be achieved, adding: "We haven't forecast full capacity flows for several months now."
On June 17, Enterprise officials said they planned to have raised Nelson's output to around 100,000 bpd by about June 24 with further increases in subsequent days.

Corrosion was discovered in the compressor during scheduled maintenance, which ended on June 16, and officials have said it would delay a return to full output and lead to a shortfall in production of around 700,000 barrels.
End-June loadings from the Forties system, which the Nelson field feeds, have already been hit by a slower than anticipated return from maintenance at the Scott field.
Traders said the equivalent of one cargo had been subtracted from the Forties schedule because of difficulties at Scott and the woes at Nelson would cause further June delays and trim July loadings.
A June 28-30 Forties cargo has already been cancelled, though the cause has not been specified.
